summary: Defines DHCP options that let a CAPWAP wireless termination point discover the Access Controllers it should connect to. This is a Proposed Standard.

eli5.summary: A new wifi box needs to find its boss computer. This memo lets the box ask the network's address-giving service, which tells it where the bosses are.

questions: how does a capwap access point find its controller
what is the capwap dhcp option
how does a wireless access point find its controller
subtitle: How a wireless access point learns, through DHCP, which controllers it should connect to.

tldr.problem: A CAPWAP Wireless Termination Point (WTP) needs to find the Access Controllers (ACs) it should connect to before it can start the CAPWAP discovery process.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a DHCPv4 option (code 138) and a DHCPv6 option (code 52) that carry an ordered list of AC addresses from the DHCP server to the WTP.
tldr.outcome: A WTP can learn its controllers from ordinary DHCP, but because DHCP is usually unauthenticated, the option should not be the only discovery method in security-sensitive networks.

today: RFC 5417 is a Proposed Standard and the unit metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It defines the DHCP options for the CAPWAP protocol in RFC 5415.

sections.title: Why DHCP Carries Controller Addresses
sections.content:
The CAPWAP protocol (RFC 5415) lets a Wireless Termination Point (WTP) connect to an Access Controller (AC). Before the CAPWAP discovery process starts, the WTP may use one of many methods to identify the right AC. One of these methods is DHCP.

This RFC defines two options for that purpose: the CAPWAP AC DHCPv4 option and the CAPWAP AC DHCPv6 option. It uses terminology from RFC 3753, RFC 2131, RFC 3315 and RFC 5415.
sections.eli5: Before a wifi box can talk to its boss computer, it has to know where the boss is. One way to find out is to ask the network's address helper.

sections.title: The DHCPv4 Option
sections.content:
The DHCPv4 option carries a list of 32-bit IPv4 addresses, each naming a CAPWAP AC available to the WTP. The option-code is OPTION_CAPWAP_AC_V4 (138). The option-length gives the length of the address list in octets and MUST be a multiple of four.

The ACs are listed in order of preference for use by the WTP.
sections.eli5: The helper writes a list of boss addresses on a card, with the favorite first. Each address is the same size, so the card is easy to read.

sections.title: The DHCPv6 Option
sections.content: The DHCPv6 option works the same way but carries 128-bit IPv6 addresses. The option-code is OPTION_CAPWAP_AC_V6 (52), and the option-length MUST be a multiple of sixteen. Again the ACs are listed in order of preference.
sections.eli5: It is the same card, but for the newer, longer kind of address, so each entry takes more room.

sections.title: Client and Server Behavior
sections.content:
A DHCP client acting on behalf of a WTP MUST request the option in a Parameter Request List Option, as described in RFC 2131 and RFC 2132 for DHCPv4, and in RFC 3315 for DHCPv6.

A server returns the option if its policy is configured appropriately and it has a list of CAPWAP AC addresses. A WTP that receives the option MAY use the addresses to locate an AC, and SHOULD try them in the order listed. RFC 5415 provides guidance on the WTP's discovery process.
sections.eli5: The box has to ask for the list, and the helper only answers if it has one. Then the box tries the bosses from the top of the list down.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
If an adversary modifies a DHCP server response or inserts its own, a WTP could be led to a rogue AC, possibly one that intercepts call requests or denies service. CAPWAP's use of Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS) MUST be used to authenticate the CAPWAP peers when the session is established.

In most networks, the DHCP exchange that delivers these options happens before network access authentication and is neither integrity protected nor origin authenticated. In security-sensitive environments the options SHOULD NOT be the only method used to pick an AC. RFC 5415 defines other discovery procedures a WTP MAY use.
sections.eli5: A trickster could slip the box a fake list of bosses. So the box should check who it is really talking to and not trust the list blindly.

sections.title: IANA Assignments
sections.content: IANA assigned DHCPv4 option code 138 to OPTION_CAPWAP_AC_V4 and DHCPv6 option code 52 to OPTION_CAPWAP_AC_V6.
sections.eli5: Each option got its own official number so nobody else uses it for something different.
